reader: source-only reader (publisher pictures + page facts); no analyzer, solver or model output was run or seen
frontHow: The entrance door of room 1 opens through the bottom wall of the ground plan into the recessed corner porch (entry arrows at the bottom-right corner), the page says the ridge is perpendicular to the road, and the elevation with the entrance door is the narrow gable wall.

overall.includes: Width 8.80 is the gable (front) wall. Depth 11.20 is the walled house; the plan's overall 15.20 and the page text 'dlugosc budynku 15,20 m' take in MORE: a 4.00 deep open rear terrace with a screen wall. The upper floor is wider than the ground floor: a box projecting 1.30 over the left wall makes it 10.10 (printed on the attic plan); that overhang is not in the 8.80.

outlineNote: A narrow rectangle 8.80 x 11.20 with its gable to the front; the front-right corner is cut out as a recessed entrance porch under the main roof (one corner column), and the rear terrace is open.
uncertain: The four elevation pictures are captioned only 'Elewacja domu Wena - 1..4'; sides were assigned from the plans: 1 = FRONT (gable with entrance door and slot window), 2 = RIGHT (long side with the porch recess at its left end and roof windows), 3 = REAR (gable with the living-room glazing), 4 = LEFT (long side with the timber box).
No section is published; only the page's building height 8.46 m is available, and what it is measured from is not stated.

The LEFT dormer is a flat-roofed timber-clad box (attic room 5, 4.50 long) that projects 1.30 beyond the left wall and overhangs the terrace doors; it is recorded as a WALL dormer of form OTHER rather than as a separate body.

RIGHT ground count of 3 = two windows (room 1 and room 7) plus the small window of room 4 that faces right inside the entrance porch recess; on the elevation the recess shows only as a dark slot, so 2 is possible.
RIGHT roofWindows 3 = two roof windows low on the slope plus one small one near the ridge, which may be a roof-access hatch.
The upper gable openings (two on the front, two on the rear) have railings in front of them and no balcony slab on the attic plan; they are taken as French balconies, so balconies is 0.
REAR ground count of 2 = the room-7 window and the large glazed unit with a door in the living room, counted as one opening.
The stone-clad block beside the rear terrace on elevations 2 and 4 is the terrace screen wall, not part of the walled house.
